name: Sanofi India Ltd
title: Sanofi India Ltd - 500674 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Diabetes growing ~14% in Q2 FY27 with insulin share strong, but partnership-channel sales are flat at 2% growth and management does not expect industry growth in 2026, so the top line is weak and mainly diabetes-driven.

triggers.label: One-off safety stock base effect in Q1
triggers.quote: the first year, the agreement with the partners that we start building their inventory -- safety inventory in Q1 in 2025

red_flags.label: Management does not expect industry growth in 2026
red_flags.quote: maybe 2026, I don't I'm not expecting that we'll reach the industry growth

evasions.quote: 2027, this is what we -- where we are evaluating right now.

summary.headline: Sanofi India Q1 FY27 PBT before exceptionals rose 19% to INR 112 crore on opex cuts, while diabetes grew ~14% in the quarter and total sales grew only ~2%.
summary.overview: Q2 CY2026 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) showed a stronger quarter, with PBT before exceptional items up 19% YoY from INR 94 crore to INR 112 crore and margin rising from 24% to 27% of net sales. Diabetes grew close to 14% in the quarter and 17% in H1, led by Toujeo and Soliqua and aided by public-sector expansion. Partnership-related sales (CV, CNS) remained weak because of a prior-year safety-stock build and one-off return adjustments, and the company said 2026 growth in that business would not reach industry levels. H1 total income was down about 4% and revenue about 2%, with export losses in Australia and other products.

financial_highlights.change: Export losing ground; domestic and export both cited
Q1 partnership transition impact not fully offset

financial_highlights.metric: Profit before tax and exceptional items (Q2)
Overall Company sales growth in Q2 per management (partnership-affected)

segments.name: Diabetes (Lantus, Toujeo, Soliqua)
segments.commentary: Grew close to 14% in Q2 and 17% in H1; Lantus value share ~47%, Toujeo second-generation basal insulin grew 11% in value, basal analog share ~58% by value and ~61% by volume, Soliqua up 16% quarter-on-quarter.

segments.name: Partnership portfolio (CV, CNS, OAD)
segments.commentary: Q2 growth around 2%, below management's expectation; Q1 hit by safety-stock build in Q1 2025 and one-off sales-return adjustments. Amaryl/OAD sales-out via Emcure reportedly tracking market growth.

segments.name: Export
segments.commentary: Down about 2% in Q2; Australia hit by heavy competition in mature products, partly offset by Goa site specialisation and wins in France, Italy, Turkey and Russia.

segments.name: Other operating income (consumer health services)
segments.commentary: Lower because certain services provided to consumer health in the past are no longer provided.

guidance_outlook: Management does not expect partnership business to reach industry growth in 2026; 2027 under evaluation.
Management expects diabetes momentum to continue into H2 but would not commit to 14%, saying it could be 10-15%.
Dividend payout expected to be at least at last year's level, subject to Board decision; no firm commitment.
Opex discipline expected to continue (quarter -5%, H1 -15%) without affecting top line.
No buyback in current strategy; proposals discussed by Board but not in plan.
capex_capacity: Goa site being positioned as specialised manufacturing hub for certain products for worldwide supply; one product already won and other actions pending.
Some products previously outsourced to CMOs are being brought back in-house to increase volume at the site.
demand_pricing: Insulin market: management believes insulin demand will hold despite GLP-1 and that analog segment continues at double-digit growth; higher single-digit growth overall expected long-term.
Novo Nordisk's once-weekly Awiqli seen as addressing a different patient profile; management says no major shift expected but will watch for one quarter.
Public sector expansion (CGHS, ESI, Railways, state and Army accounts) has driven close to 70% growth in that channel for Toujeo and Soliqua.
Partnership competition described as aggressive in generic CV/CNS/OAD segments.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the partnership business growing so slowly and when will it catch up with the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q1 weakness to Q1 2025 safety-stock build and one-off sales returns; Q2 at ~2% was below expectation. Industry-level growth not expected in 2026, with 2027 under evaluation. Denied that Emcure or Cipla are sidelining Sanofi products.

qa_highlights.question: Is 14% diabetes growth sustainable and are there new segments beyond diabetes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would not commit to 14%, citing 10-15% range; cardiovascular and CNS partnerships remain strategic. Large underdiagnosed patient pool (~100 million cited) gives room for growth. No new parent products identified yet beyond diabetes devices/AI platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Will dividend payout remain healthy post-demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Cannot commit ahead of Board decision; expected payout not lower than last year, supported by cash generation (+34%).

qa_highlights.question: How will Novo's once-weekly insulin affect the franchise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees limited shift as patient profiles differ; once-weekly may bring non-insulin-treated patients into insulin; will assess over the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Losses in Australia offset by wins in France, Italy, Turkey and Russia; Goa site specialisation and CMO-outsourced products being brought back.

qa_highlights.question: Would the company consider an open-market buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Not part of current strategy; any such proposal would be discussed by the Board.

risks_watch: Partnership (CV, CNS, OAD) growth remains weak at ~2%, with no firm timeline for industry-level growth.
Export revenue declining; Australia competition in mature products persists.
Whether diabetes growth of ~14-17% holds in H2 as the public-sector channel and Novo's once-weekly entry evolve.
H1 total income and PBT still down YoY, so the margin gains depend on continued opex cuts.
Dividend payout commitment not given; Board decision pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on diabetes and margin expansion, but noticeably defensive on the partnership business, which management conceded was below its own expectations and gave no firm recovery timeline for. Answers on payout and buyback were non-committal.
key_quotes: If you look at the quarter two results, closer to 14% double-digit growth, powered by innovative portfolio, which is both Toujeo and Soliqua.

adds.what: Goa site repositioned as specialised manufacturing hub for certain products; some CMO-outsourced products being brought back in-house

growth.why: Management guided diabetes momentum into H2 (could be 10-15%) and Goa in-sourcing, but partnership business will not reach industry growth in 2026, export is losing ground, and H1 revenue is down about 2%, so overall growth is modest with no committed capacity timeline or capex figure.
